arxiv-2109-13586.title: Dynamics in Coded Edge Computing for IoT: A Fractional Evolutionary Game Approach
arxiv-2109-13586.creator: Yue Han, Dusit Niyato, Cyril Leung, Chunyan Miao, Dong In Kim
arxiv-2109-13586.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yue Han, Dusit Niyato, Cyril Leung, Chunyan Miao, Dong In Kim. Recently, coded distributed computing (CDC), with advantages in intensive computation and reduced latency, has attracted a lot of research interest for edge computing, in particular, IoT applications, including IoT data pre-processing and data analytics. Nevertheless, it can be challenging for edge infrastructure providers (EIPs) with limited edge resources to support IoT applications performed in a CDC approach in edge networks, given the additional computational resources required by CDC.

arxiv-2206-04520.title: An FPGA-based Solution for Convolution Operation Acceleration
arxiv-2206-04520.creator: Trung Pham-Dinh, Bao Bach-Gia, Lam Luu-Trinh, Minh Nguyen-Dinh, Hai Pham-Duc, Khoa Bui-Anh, Xuan-Quang Nguyen, Cuong Pham-Quoc
arxiv-2206-04520.description: Abstract Hardware-based acceleration is an extensive attempt to facilitate many computationally-intensive mathematics operations. This paper proposes an FPGA-based architecture to accelerate the convolution operation - a complex and expensive computing step that appears in many Convolutional Neural Network models. We target the design to the standard convolution operation, intending to launch the product as an edge-AI solution.

arxiv-2302-13187.title: Tractable Diversity: Scalable Multiperspective Ontology Management via Standpoint ℰ ​ ℒ \mathcal{E\!L}
arxiv-2302-13187.creator: Lucía Gómez Álvarez and Sebastian Rudolph and Hannes Strass
arxiv-2302-13187.description: Abstract The tractability of the lightweight description logic ℰ ​ ℒ \mathcal{E\!L} has allowed for the construction of large and widely used ontologies that support semantic interoperability. However, comprehensive domains with a broad user base are often at odds with strong axiomatisations otherwise useful for inferencing, since these are usually context dependent and subject to diverging perspectives.

arxiv-2311-14825.title: Studying the phase diagram of the three-flavor Schwinger model in the presence of a chemical potential with measurement- and gate-based quantum computing
arxiv-2311-14825.creator: Stephan Schuster, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Tobias Hartung, Marc-Oliver Pleinert, Joachim von Zanthier, Karl Jansen
arxiv-2311-14825.description: Abstract We propose an ansatz quantum circuit for the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), suitable for exploring the phase structure of the multi-flavor Schwinger model in the presence of a chemical potential. Our ansatz is capable of incorporating relevant model symmetries via constrains on the parameters, and can be implemented on circuit-based as well as measurement-based quantum devices.

arxiv-2401-05218.title: Invariant Causal Prediction with Local Models
arxiv-2401-05218.creator: Alexander Mey, Rui Manuel Castro
arxiv-2401-05218.description: Abstract We consider the task of identifying the causal parents of a target variable among a set of candidates from observational data. Our main assumption is that the candidate variables are observed in different environments which may, under certain assumptions, be regarded as interventions on the observed system.

arxiv-2406-08193.title: Minimal Communication-Cost Statistical Learning
arxiv-2406-08193.description: Abstract A client device which has access to n n training data samples needs to obtain a statistical hypothesis or model W W and then to send it to a remote server. The client and the server devices share some common randomness sequence as well as a prior on the hypothesis space.

arxiv-2510-14930.title: VT-Refine: Learning Bimanual Assembly with Visuo-Tactile Feedback via Simulation Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2510-14930.creator: Binghao Huang, Iretiayo Akinola, Wei Yang, Balakumar Sundaralingam, Rowland O’Flaherty, Dieter Fox, Xiaolong Wang, Arsalan Mousavian, Yu-Wei Chao, Yunzhu Li
arxiv-2510-14930.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Binghao Huang, Iretiayo Akinola, Wei Yang, Balakumar Sundaralingam, Rowland O’Flaherty, Dieter Fox, Xiaolong Wang, Arsalan Mousavian, Yu-Wei Chao, Yunzhu Li. Humans excel at bimanual assembly tasks by adapting to rich tactile feedback—a capability that remains difficult to replicate in robots through behavioral cloning alone, due to the suboptimality and limited diversity of human demonstrations. In this work, we present VT-Refine, a visuo-tactile policy learning framework that combines real-world demonstrations, high-fidelity tactile simulation, and reinforcement learning to tackle precise, contact-rich bimanual assembly.

pmc-11431536.title: One-Photon-Interference Quantum Secure Direct Communication
pmc-11431536.creator: Xiang-Jie Li, Min Wang, Xing-Bo Pan, Yun-Rong Zhang, Gui-Lu Long, Osamu Hirota
pmc-11431536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) is a quantum communication paradigm that transmits confidential messages directly using quantum states. Measurement-device-independent (MDI) QSDC protocols can eliminate the security loopholes associated with measurement devices. To enhance the practicality and performance of MDI-QSDC protocols, we propose a one-photon-interference MDI QSDC (OPI-QSDC) protocol which transcends the need for quantum memory, ideal single-photon sources, or entangled light sources. The security of our OPI-QSDC protocol has also been analyzed using quantum wiretap channel theory.

Methods: The method addresses the analytical challenge posed by the significantly different concentration ranges of α-TOH (µmol/L) and its metabolites (nmol/L).

pmc-12768824.title: OP29 Persistence Of Biologic And Targeted Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs In The Treatment Of Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Cohort Study
pmc-12768824.creator: Natália Brandão, Gerusa Oliveira, Marina Garcia, Bárbara Alvernaz, Francisco Acurcio, Augusto Guerra, Juliana Álvares-Teodoro
pmc-12768824.description: IntroductionRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease affecting the joints. Biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs) have expanded the therapeutic armamentarium for RA and significantly changed its management. However, there are still unmet needs for patients who do not respond to treatment.

pmc-13103877.title: Real-World Impact of Insurance Changes on Long-acting Cabotegravir Plus Rilpivirine Delivery
pmc-13103877.creator: Jennifer M Davis, Jennifer O’Neill, Elizabeth Lyden, Sara H Bares
pmc-13103877.description: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine offers an alternative to daily oral antiretroviral therapy, but insurance-related barriers can disrupt implementation. We examined the frequency and impact of insurance changes in a United States cohort and found that nearly half of patients experienced insurance changes, which could lead to delayed injections.

pmc-13430498.title: Mechanistic insights into ferroptosis and its therapeutic potential in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13430498.creator: Fan Yang, Zhongjie Li, Bao Zheng
pmc-13430498.description: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, distinct from apoptosis and necrosis. It has been confirmed as a key regulator in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study systematically elucidates three interconnected regulatory networks of ferroptosis—metabolic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental—and proposes a closed-loop regulatory model integrating these dimensions.

pmc-13543965.title: An Estrogen–IL-33 Circuit in Aortic Fibroblasts Underlies Sex Differences in Tregs in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
pmc-13543965.creator: Wangling Hu, Jingyong Li, Luna Zhai, Zhuo Chen, Linwei Ye, Ni Xia, Tingting Tang, Shaofang Nie, Min Zhang, Jiao Jiao, Bingjie Lv, Fen Yang, Yuzhi Lu, Lingfeng Zha, Muyang Gu, Xiajun Hu, Shuang Wen, Dan Li, Desheng Hu, Weimin Wang, Chen Chen, Qing K Wang, Zhilei Shan, Yong Ji, Xiang Cheng
pmc-13543965.description: Visual AbstractKey words: abdominal aortic aneurysm, IL-33, NF-κB, regulatory T cell, sex COMPETENCY IN MEDICAL KNOWLEDGE: This study advances our understanding of sex-dependent immune regulation in AAA, especially Tregs. We identify an estrogen/ERα/NF-κB/IL-33 axis driving Treg sex dimorphism. It highlights sex as a critical biological variable in vascular inflammation and aneurysm pathogenesis.
